S78.01.note: The resolver itself is code in apps/mobile/src/lib/capabilities.tsx (useCapability); there is no screen for it.
steps: Tap the model name beside the + button in a chat's composer.
Pick a model that has reasoning effort levels, then close the picker.
Pick a model that has none, then reopen the picker and look for the Effort section.
Compare what appears and disappears with Expected.
S78.01.where: Inner rule. Its effect shows on the model picker and the chat composer controls (see S78.02).

S78.02.note: The With thinking switch appears on a model row when that row is expanded; the exact expand gesture was not traced in the code.
steps: Open a chat, then tap the model name beside the + button in the composer.
Pick a model that has reasoning effort levels and check that an Effort slider appears in the picker.
Close the picker and look at the right end of the composer toolbar for the effort button.
Pick a model with no effort levels and check that the effort button is gone. Compare with Expected.
S78.02.where: Chat > model name beside the + button in the composer > model picker > Effort section and With thinking switch.

labels.text: isn’t an accepted file type. Attach a JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP image instead.

S78.03.needs: a file the app should refuse, such as one with an unusual type
S78.03.note: The code checks file type and size against the send destination (local or cloud), not the selected model; a model-based rule was not found in the attachment code.
steps: Open a chat and tap the + button labelled Add to chat in the composer.
Tap File and choose a file type the app does not accept.
Look for the message that says the file isn’t an accepted file type and asks for a JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP image instead.
Switch to another model and repeat. Compare with Expected.
S78.03.where: Chat > + (Add to chat) > File or Photos.

S78.04.note: Removal of unsupported levels from the request happens in the code, not on screen; only the slider options are visible.
steps: Tap the model name beside the + button in the composer.
Pick a model with effort levels and read the Effort slider labels (for example Direct, Brief, Quick, Balanced, Deep, Extended, Maximum).
Pick a different model and check that the slider now shows only the levels that model supports.
Open Settings, then General, and find Default effort. Compare with Expected.
S78.04.where: Chat > model name beside + > model picker > Effort slider; also Settings > Device > General > Default effort.

S78.06.needs: an account whose plan includes video generation
S78.06.note: The duration hint text is built from the model data, so its exact wording varies.
steps: Open a chat and tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Tap Create video. It appears only when the account plan and the video model allow it.
Look for the Aspect ratio heading and the Quality heading with their options; quality rows may show hints such as a duration in seconds.
Change the aspect ratio, or pick another media model if one is offered, and compare the options with Expected.
S78.06.where: Chat > + (Add to chat) > Create video (or Create image) > Aspect ratio and Quality rows.

S78.07.note: The server-side check on the chat route cannot be seen from the app; only the in-app check is visible.
steps: Sign in with a Free account, or with an account on a lower plan.
Tap the model name beside the + button in the composer.
Look for model rows that show Not included in plan (or Sign in required when signed out).
Compare with Expected.
S78.07.where: Chat > model name beside + > model picker, rows marked Not included in plan or Sign in required.

S78.08.note: The page reads its numbers from the server; the tester cannot see the server figure directly, only the displayed one.
steps: Sign in, open the drawer and tap Settings.
Find the Cloud group and tap Usage.
Read the Credit balances and Resets sections and the This month section, including the used or remaining figures.
Compare the remaining allowance shown with Expected.

S78.09.needs: a member account in a workspace, and an administrator who can switch a feature off
S78.09.note: No mobile screen to set workspace policy was found; the policy is applied by the server.
steps: Sign in as a member of a workspace where an administrator has turned a feature off.
Try to use that feature from the chat composer or its menu.
Look for the title Turned off by your organization on the blocked screen and compare with Expected.
S78.09.where: Set by a workspace administrator on the server. A member sees the copy Turned off by your organization on a blocked feature.

S78.10.needs: two accounts in the same workspace: one member, and one owner or admin
S78.10.note: The server also refuses role changes from non-admins; that refusal is not visible on screen.
steps: Sign in, open the drawer, tap Settings, then tap Workspace under the Account group.
As a plain member, look at the member list: no Change role button should be shown.
Sign in as a workspace owner or admin, reopen Workspace, and look for Change role on another member.
Open the role dialog as an owner and check for Transfer ownership. Compare with Expected.

labels.text: Only use AI providers based in the US

S78.11.needs: a Cloud-mode account on a plan that includes the US-only setting
S78.11.note: The eligible plans list is set in the shared types; the tester needs an account on one of those plans.
steps: Sign in to Cloud mode, open the drawer and tap Settings.
Under Assistant, tap Privacy.
Look for the switch Only use AI providers based in the US. It appears only in Cloud mode for eligible plans.
Turn the switch on, leave the screen, come back and check that it stays on. Compare with Expected.
S78.11.where: Drawer > Settings > Assistant > Privacy > Only use AI providers based in the US.

S78.12.needs: a fresh install or cleared app data, so the age check runs again
S78.12.note: The minimum age depends on the device time zone (ageGate.ts); the way to clear a recorded refusal was not traced in the UI.
steps: Use a fresh install or clear the app data so no age was recorded.
On the Your age screen, type an age below the minimum shown in the subtitle in the Enter your age field.
Tap Continue.
Look for the Age requirement screen and its refusal message. Compare with Expected.
S78.12.where: First launch, on the age screen titled Your age (before sign-in). Refusal shows the Age requirement screen.

S78.14.needs: a desktop app with AGI installed, paired or not, and optionally a second device
S78.14.note: Plan-based removal of Remote is also checked on this screen (planLacksRemoteControl); that is a separate gate.
steps: Sign in, open the drawer and tap AGI Code.
If no computer is paired, tap Add device in the devices section.
Read the connection status line: Not connected when nothing is paired, or the desktop name with offline when it is not reachable.
Tap Scan QR Code if shown. Compare the status with Expected while the desktop app is closed and then open.
S78.14.where: Drawer > AGI Code > Add device (opens the Remote pairing screen).

S78.15.needs: none for viewing; a phone with enough free storage to download
S78.15.note: The runtime check itself is in model-picker/service.ts; the tester sees its result as the badge.
steps: Tap the model name beside the + button in the composer.
Look for the On device group heading.
Read the badge on each on-device model: Download (not installed), Ready (installed), Retry (download failed), or Device (this device cannot run it).
Tap a Download model and compare the result with Expected.
S78.15.where: Chat > model name beside + > model picker > On device group.

labels.text: It’s paused while we fix an issue and will come back without an update.

S78.16.needs: an operator who can switch a feature off on the server
S78.16.note: The tester cannot switch an operator flag, so the temporary case may not be reproducible from the app alone.
steps: Only an operator can switch a feature off on the server, so this step needs that switch.
Open the gated feature while the switch is on and read the title and body.
Look for the body It’s paused while we fix an issue and will come back without an update. That is the temporary case.
Compare with the plan case, which says Not included in your plan, and with Expected.
S78.16.where: Shown on a gated screen when an operator switch is on, or when a plan closes the feature. The two cases show different copy.

S78.17.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account; a second account on a plan without voice to see the voice button hidden
S78.17.note: The voice button hiding rule is in ChatInput.tsx (voiceAllowed) and needs a plan without voice to check.
steps: Open a chat with a signed-in Cloud account and look at the right end of the composer toolbar.
Pick a model with effort levels and check that the effort button (showing a level such as Balanced) appears.
Pick a model without effort levels and check that the button is gone, not greyed out.
Compare with Expected.
S78.17.where: Chat > composer toolbar: the effort button appears only for models that have effort levels; the voice button appears only when voice is allowed.

S78.18.note: The text Opens plan upgrade options is only an accessibility hint and is not visible on screen.
steps: Sign in on a Free account, then tap the model name beside the + button.
Look for model rows that are greyed out and show Not included in plan under the name.
Tap a greyed row and compare what happens with Expected.
S78.18.where: Chat > model name beside + > model picker > rows that are greyed out with the reason Not included in plan.

labels.text: Start a new chat for this model

S78.19.needs: a Free account and a chat that already uses one provider
S78.19.note: Store purchases are off in this build (storePurchases.json nativePurchases false), so the alert and paywall show no plan name and no upgrade button; the View upgrade options label only appears when purchases are on.
steps: Sign in on a Free account and open a chat that already uses one provider.
Tap the model name beside the + button and choose a model from a different provider.
Read the alert Start a new chat for this model and its message.
Check whether a plan name or an upgrade button is shown. Compare with Expected.
S78.19.where: Chat > model name beside + > choose a model from another provider mid-chat > alert Start a new chat for this model. Also Not included in your plan on the paywall sheet.

labels.text: Used for voice input and audio recording.

S78.21.note: The prompt shown at first use of voice is a separate screen (app/(app)/voice.tsx); it was not traced in full.
steps: Open Settings from the drawer and tap Permissions under the Device group.
Read the rows Microphone, Speech Recognition, Camera and Photos & Files with their one-line descriptions.
Tap Microphone and read what it is used for before any system prompt.
Compare with Expected.

S78.22.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with image generation
S78.22.note: The full message is built from the model name and the capable model list in resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts; the search fragment cannot edit an attached image is in that file. Path steps are inferred from the code, not run.
steps: Open a chat, tap the + button labelled Add to chat and tap Create image.
Attach a photo with Photos.
Switch the image model to one that cannot edit attached images.
Send a prompt and read the message that says the model cannot edit the attached image and asks you to pick another image model or remove the attachment. Compare with Expected.
S78.22.where: Chat > + (Add to chat) > Create image > attach a photo as a reference, then choose an image model that cannot edit.

labels.text: Turned off for your account. You can turn it on when you send.

S78.24.needs: a signed-in account; an on-device model installed for the on-device path
S78.24.note: The picker offers on-device and AGI Cloud models only; no own-key (bring your own key) choice was found in the mobile picker.
steps: Tap the model name beside the + button in the composer.
Look at the On device group and pick a model there; its badge shows its install state.
Pick a cloud model and read its detail line, which names the provider.
If a provider is turned off for the account, look for the note Turned off for your account. You can turn it on when you send. Compare with Expected.
S78.24.where: Chat > model name beside + > model picker > On device group versus AGI Cloud models.

S78.26.note: The request filter lives in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts and cannot be seen from the app.
steps: Pick a model that has no effort levels, then look at the composer toolbar.
Check that no effort button is shown, which means no effort value is offered for that model.
Compare with Expected.
S78.26.where: Inner rule. The removal of unsupported parameters happens in the server request processor, so it is seen only as the model's controls being absent.

S78.28.needs: a second device or the web to change the plan or setting
S78.28.note: The refresh is in apps/mobile/src/lib/capabilities.tsx (AppState change to active); the change itself must be made outside the app.
steps: Sign in and note which gated controls are on, such as the effort button or the Remote entry.
Change the plan or a setting for that account on the web, then send the app to the background and bring it back.
Reopen the model picker and the composer and check whether the controls changed without restarting. Compare with Expected.
S78.28.where: Inner rule. The app refreshes capability switches when it returns to the foreground and when the signed-in state changes; the effect shows on gated controls.
